name: Kiama Blowhole & Coast Walk
blurb: Headlands, sea stacks and basalt columns, ending at the famous Kiama Blowhole.
weatherNote: Open headlands with little shade: start early on hot days. Skip it in rain, when the tracks get slippery and the views vanish.
gettingThere: South Coast Line train from Central to Minnamurra (≈ 2 hr 10, hourly). Walk south to the Blowhole, then it's 15 min to Kiama station for the train home.
newcomerTip: The Blowhole is best when the swell comes from the southeast. On Fridays and weekends Opal caps your whole day at $9.65, so the long train trip costs less than you'd think.

back.text: It's one way. From the Blowhole, walk to Kiama station (≈ 15 min) and take the South Coast Line straight back to Central (≈ 2 hr 10–2 hr 20). Trains run about hourly.

notes: There's parking at Blowhole Point, by the Visitor Information Centre.
It's a one-way walk: park in Kiama and take the train two stops north to Minnamurra to start.

routes.ride: Not practical from the city: it's a long, expensive ride. Take the train.

visit.bestTime: Catch a morning train and start walking by 11am, so you reach the Blowhole by mid-afternoon with time for lunch in Kiama.
visit.hours: The walk is always open. Kiama Visitor Information Centre at Blowhole Point is open daily 9am to 5pm, except Christmas Day.
facilities: Toilets at Blowhole Point, always open
Diggies café beside the Visitor Information Centre at Blowhole Point
Whale-watching platform at Minnamurra headland (May to November)
visit.access: Not suitable end to end for prams or wheelchairs: Kiama's walk guide lists loose surfaces, steep sections and beach walking. Blowhole Point has accessible viewing platforms.
safety: Stay behind the fences at the Blowhole: big waves wash over the rock shelf
Keep back from cliff edges on the headlands
Signage is limited: follow the walk markers and check the map
